To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of nanoparticles to the hydroponics solution surrounding the roots of maize seedlings inhibits leaf growth, and that the mechanism of this inhibition appears to involve a rapid reduction in root hydraulic conductivity due to a physical blockage of apoplastic water flow through cell wall pores.

colloidal suspensions (0.1-1.0% w/w) of inorganic nanoparticle materials of natural or industrially produced origin can inhibit water flow through the root cell wall, reduce leaf growth and transpiretion and, in the case of soil-grown maize, reduce shoot growth over several weeks.
the presence of colloidal suspensions containing nanoparticles in the root environment can rapidly inhibit leaf growth and photosynthesis by interfering with water transport through the cell wall.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical effects of nanoparticles on water transport through root cell walls and the associated leaf effects.
the physical rather than the toxic effects of colloidal nanoparticles on water transport in plants.
the potential of colloidal suspensions in irrigation water to interfere with root water transport and cause associated leaf responses in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physical presence of nanoparticles in the external water supply can interfere with water flow through root apoplast and inhibit leaf growth and photosynthesis.

colloidal suspensions can interfere with water transport in maize seedlings via rapid physical effects on root cell wall pores, and the resulting leaf responses are consistent with the hypothesis that the root water transport pathway is a major target of nanoparticle effects on plants.
nanoparticle treatments can rapidly inhibit water flow through root cell wall pores, and that this can cause a rapid inhibition of transpiration and leaf growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nanoparticle-induced leaf responses can involve physical rather than toxic effects, and that these can be detected at the root level.

nanoparticle suspensions can rapidly inhibit root water flow via physical effects on apoplastic water transport, and that this is associated with a rapid inhibition of leaf growth and transpirational water loss.

the nanoparticle effects on water transport in the apoplastic pathway of the root were rapid, reversible and non-toxic, and that these nanoparticle effects were the major factor responsible for the observed inhibition of leaf growth and transpiring leaf area in the intact maize plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of nanoparticles in the external water supply can rapidly inhibit water transport through the apoplast, and this effect may be relevant in the field.
nanoparticle-induced inhibition of water transport can occur in a matter of minutes and can be rapid and substantial, and that this effect is not restricted to the laboratory.

the physical properties of colloidal nanoparticle suspensions, including their size and concentration, can be more important than their chemistry or toxicity in determining their effects on plant water transport and growth.
